clue.text: Bookmaker's secret arrangement secures advantage

indicators.note: secures means holds inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other
an arrangement of the word secret puts its letters into a new order

parts.note: VAN is short for advantage, the tennis score after deuce

explanation.surface: A bookie's hidden deal includes some advantage for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' gives CERTES, which 'secures' the tennis term. A book-maker here is an author, not a bookie: Cervantes wrote Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes was the Spanish novelist who wrote Don Quixote, so he literally made books.

clue.text: Get into trouble as Christian in Africa — one's arrested

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the Christian holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a Copt is a member of the Coptic Church of Egypt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Christian in Africa runs into trouble when one of the faithful is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is one is: I is held by COPT. 'as' is a link. Cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop it is British slang meaning to be punished or get into serious trouble.

clue.text: Cheese dish with Brie chewed and eaten by vermin

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rat is a classic example of vermin

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the word Brie is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheese dish ruined after rats have gnawed through the Brie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges BRIE to REBI, which is 'eaten by' RAT. Rarebit is Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted seasoned cheese on toast, a British cheese dish.

clue.text: Union character not opening basket on nice beach

indicators.note: not opening means without its first letter

parts.note: a hamper is a large wicker basket
sand stands for a beach, here a pleasant one

explanation.surface: A character in a trade union refuses to open his picnic basket on a lovely beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union character' is the symbol that joins: the & sign. 'not opening' removes the H from HAMPER, leaving AMPER, which sits 'on' (before) SAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the typographical character meaning 'and', which joins or unites words.

clue.text: Infallible memory for cricket scores?

parts.note: a perfect memory, playfully read as being able to recall every cricket total ever made

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means perfect recollection of everything, and a total is a team's score in cricket.

clue.text: Outlawed weapon seen to rise and fall

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: poison gas is a weapon banned by international conventions

explanation.surface: A banned weapon is seen to go up and come down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to rise' turns GAS upwards in this down entry; 'and' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to sink or droop downwards.

clue.text: Man — a short island

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: Staffa is a small Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person as one short island, perhaps in a geography quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a noun (or the Isle of Man beside 'island'), but it is the verb: to man a desk. 'short' removes the last A from STAFFA.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a post or office is to staff it, supplying the people who run it.

clue.text: Son takes step into room

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A boy steps into a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... into' is only a link: the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of free area or capacity is space.

clue.text: A cinema reel, bloody poor

indicators.note: reel means to whirl or stagger, so the letters of cinema are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a film reel as dreadfully poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' looks like a film reel but means stagger, jumbling the second piece. The definition means poor in blood, and also feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic means lacking red blood cells, so the blood is poor; it also means feeble.

clue.text: No benefit abandoning this vessel if there's a fire

definitions.text: No benefit abandoning this vessel if there's a fire

parts.words: No benefit abandoning this vessel if there's a fire
parts.note: alludes to the saying about jumping out of one cooking pot straight into the flames, no better off

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says out of the frying pan into the fire: escaping one trouble only to meet a worse one.

clue.text: Bedding in oil plant, gently press down low bank

indicators.note: bedding one thing in another sets it firmly inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to pat is to press down gently with the hand
rape is the plant grown for rapeseed oil

explanation.surface: Gardening instructions: settle an oilseed plant into the soil and press it down gently.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as planting advice; 'Bedding in' is the container signal, and 'low bank' is the definition, not a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall or earth bank along the edge of a roof, bridge or trench.

clue.text: Old woman nervous heading off for store

parts.note: gran is an informal word for grandmother, an old woman

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter, the head of the word

parts.note: wary means cautious and nervous

explanation.surface: A nervous elderly lady sets off for the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like setting out on a journey; it removes the W from WARY to leave ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for threshed grain.

clue.text: Row across black river

indicators.note: across here means stretched over, so the row goes around the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone rows across a dark river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as the verb to paddle a boat; it is the noun, a tier, which 'across' wraps around B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: Say, Don Giovanni perishes priest comes round with absolution at the end

indicators.note: comes round means surrounds, so the priest encloses the other piece

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest or monk
dies means perishes

indicators.note: at the end picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Don Giovanni dies in the opera, and a priest arrives to absolve him at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Don Giovanni as an example; 'comes round' is the container signal and 'at the end' supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni, Mozart's seducer, is the classic example of a womaniser or charmer of women.

clue.text: Miss Miller features holding a series of flower arrangements

parts.note: Daisy Miller is the heroine of Henry James's novella of that name

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: chins are facial features

explanation.surface: A Miss Miller arranges a series of flower displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside CHINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy chains are strings of daisies linked together by their stems, a simple flower arrangement.

clue.text: Badly affected by dose of illegal drug

definitions.meaning: a region hard ... by floods is badly affected by them
slang for a single dose of a drug

explanation.definitionFit: Hard hit means badly affected, and in drug slang a hit is a single dose.

clue.text: Desperately anxious, in terrible danger, hid

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: In terrible danger, someone hides, desperately anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DANGER and HID together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hag-ridden means tormented, as if haunted by a witch, so harassed and anxious.

clue.text: Competition for boats as race up Cam is organised

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat race up the River Cam, in Cambridge, is being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race up Cam is' is the fodder, and 'organised' rearranges it; 'as' is only a link. The Cam is the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The America's Cup is the famous international yacht racing trophy and competition.

clue.text: Past the stage of enjoying Latin

definitions.text: Past the stage of enjoying Latin

parts.words: Past the stage of enjoying Latin
parts.note: a Latin phrase meaning to the point of sickness, done until it stops being enjoyable

explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is a Latin tag for doing something so long it becomes sickening.

clue.text: Gorge from splendid tin over there

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
a can is a tin container
yon is an old or dialect word meaning over there

explanation.surface: A gorge reached from a splendid tin mine somewhere over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is the world's most famous gorge.

clue.text: Brisk movement inhibited by illiberal legroom

indicators.note: inhibited by means held within, so the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: A brisk walk is held back by an airline's stingy legroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across illiber-AL LEGRO-om. 'movement' is a section of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a brisk tempo, and a movement in that tempo is called an allegro.

clue.text: Stop players short

indicators.note: short means cut off before the final letter

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players

explanation.surface: A team stops playing because it is short of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like a sports team; it is a band of musicians, cut short to lose its D.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to stop or prohibit it.

clue.text: Employed by intelligence, computer studies country

indicators.note: employed by means taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brain means intelligence
IT is information technology, the school subject of computer studies

explanation.surface: A country's computer studies are put to use by its intelligence service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' looks like spies, but it is brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the country of England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: I shall fill poor land with lake, being far from well

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: heath is open uncultivated land with poor soil
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone vows to flood barren land with a lake, despite feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill' puts L inside HEATH, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is the state of being unwell, far from well.

clue.text: Call up woman to receive fine

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone phones a woman to collect a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like phoning, but it means summon to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or feeling is to call it up or summon it.

clue.text: America is to put charge on New York body

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the charge follows the other piece

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, has its headquarters in New York
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: The United States plans to bring a charge against a New York organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as an accusation but is an electrically charged particle. The Union was the name for the northern United States in the Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union is a name for the United States, especially the northern states in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Sea bird often with big ears seen in capitals

definitions.meaning: a tropical tern named for its nodding courtship display

definitions.text: often with big ears seen in capitals
definitions.meaning: Enid Blyton's toy character, constantly with his friend Big Ears, whose names are written in capitals

explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is a tropical tern, and Noddy is Enid Blyton's toy boy whose companion is Big Ears.

clue.text: Make improvements, burying last piece of yew tree

indicators.note: burying means putting deep inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to do good is to make things better

indicators.note: last piece of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A gardener improves things by burying the remains of a yew tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yew tree' looks like a phrase, but the definition is just 'tree'; 'burying' puts W, the last letter of yew, into DO GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogwood is a shrub or small tree of the genus Cornus.

clue.text: Note sounded by Homer

definitions.meaning: the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale
the exasperated exclamation of Homer Simpson in the cartoon

explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale and Homer Simpson's catchphrase of annoyance.

clue.text: Passion part of Germany had for composer

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion
a Land is one of the federal states of Germany

explanation.surface: Some part of Germany had a passion for a particular composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had for' is a link. John Ireland was an English composer of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ireland (1879-1962) was an English composer of songs, piano and orchestral music.

clue.text: The point of writing about Old English woman of sorrows

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a nib is the point of a pen used for writing

explanation.surface: An essay on the purpose of writing about a sorrowful woman in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' looks like one phrase (OE) but splits: 'about' puts O inside NIB, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children and became the emblem of grieving.

clue.text: Payment for talk stopped

parts.note: reads as a fee cancelled for a lecture, but means money paid so that someone keeps quiet

explanation.definitionFit: This is money paid as a bribe to keep someone silent about something.
